research_scope: Base-game Parallel Quest skills from PQ 48-55 selected after duplicate screening against the canonical skill index and prior research batches.

verification_audit.method: Skill identity, class, core cost data, and PQ acquisition routes were reconciled against current Xenoverse 2 skill references and independent PQ reward guides. Exact drop probabilities and version-sensitive frame data were not inferred.

records.name: Kamekameha
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 48 — 2nd World Tournament Tag Team; reward
records.skill_description: A fast Kamehameha-style beam that fires more quickly than the standard Kamehameha but cannot be charged.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 skill documentation identifies Kamekameha as Goten's Ki Blast Super, costing 100 Ki and obtained from PQ48. The documented attack is a six-hit beam with knockback; exact current damage scaling is not promoted as universal.
records.combo_notes: The uncharged, fast-firing behavior distinguishes it from the standard Kamehameha; detailed frame routes remain outside the verified scope.
records.pve_notes: A quick beam option useful when a faster activation is preferable to a chargeable Kamehameha.
records.pvp_notes: Its speed can matter for confirms, but version-specific frame advantage is intentionally unresolved.

records.name: Do or Die
records.skill_description: Strengthens the user's resolve and temporarily reduces damage taken, while producing a small close-range knockback wave on activation.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 documentation identifies Do or Die as a Power Up Super costing 100 Ki, lasting 20 seconds, and reducing incoming damage by 10 percent. The PQ49 route is independently corroborated. Exact version-specific defensive interactions are not asserted beyond the documented effect.
records.combo_notes: This is a defensive reinforcement skill rather than a conventional combo starter; activation timing should be documented separately from attack routes.
records.pve_notes: The temporary damage reduction can support sustained PvE encounters where the user expects to absorb incoming attacks.
records.pvp_notes: The activation commitment and defensive effect make timing important; no universal cancel or frame advantage is asserted.

records.name: Explosive Buu Buu Punch
records.skill_description: A short-range nine-hit punch barrage that can also be activated while jumping and provides super armor during the attack sequence.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 documentation identifies Explosive Buu Buu Punch as a 100-Ki Strike Super usable by Majin CaCs. It is documented as a nine-hit barrage with super armor and knockback. Exact current damage values are not promoted as universal.
records.combo_notes: The move's super armor and multi-hit rush behavior distinguish it from ordinary single-hit Strike Supers; detailed combo routes require separate testing.
records.pve_notes: The armor and sustained punch sequence can be relevant when trading with AI enemies, subject to stamina and matchup context.
records.pvp_notes: Super armor changes how opponents can challenge the startup, but exact armor windows and punish timings are version-sensitive.

records.name: Victory Cannon
records.skill_description: Fires a Ki wave from the user's mouth while recoil propels the user backward to create distance from the opponent.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 documentation identifies Victory Cannon as Gotenks's Ki Blast Evasive, costing 300 stamina. The attack launches nearby opponents and uses recoil to move the user backward. Exact current damage and invulnerability-frame data are intentionally unresolved.
records.combo_notes: Its defining behavior is defensive repositioning through recoil rather than a conventional offensive combo sequence.
records.pve_notes: Can create substantial separation after an unfavorable close-range exchange, making its movement component important against AI pressure.
records.pvp_notes: The recoil changes spacing after activation; exact invulnerability and punish windows should be tested per game version rather than inferred.
